_comment: Canonical schema descriptor template (schema/<name>.json). The engine treats the entire document as opaque — no field is consumed at runtime. A schema is itself a four-section element (brique/objective/functional/subjective), and its functional section holds a nested gabarit reproducing the same four sections — brique/objective/functional/subjective — but of the element this schema templates, not of the schema itself. Each key inside that nested gabarit carries either an explicit list of admissible values (drawn from the vocabulary) or no value at all when the key exists but is left open at instantiation. An optional sibling '_comment' key may accompany any field to note its expected type or intent — like every other '_'-prefixed key in this template, it documents and is stripped at instantiation, never copied into the instantiated element.

brique._comment: Required for reflexive projection (meaning queries, read.meaning). No field here is validated by the engine at runtime.

objective._comment: Optional. Projected by the reflexive meaning layer.
objective.name: <schema_name>
objective._name_note: Conventionally matches the schema filename without .json.
objective.description: One sentence describing what shape this schema constrains.

functional._comment: Opaque to the engine. Holds the nested gabarit of the templated element's own four sections — not a list-of-fields format. Wrappers and tooling may read this for validation logic.

brique._comment: The templated element's own brique section, in gabarit form. Rarely constrained by a schema in practice — most schemas leave this empty — but present for structural symmetry.
brique._key_note: Example only, remove. A key here carries either a list of admissible values for the templated element's brique.<key>, drawn from the vocabulary, or no value when the key is expected but left open.

objective._comment: The templated element's own objective section, in gabarit form.
objective._key_note: Example only, remove. Same rule as above: a list of admissible values, or no value when left open. A sibling '_comment' may document type/intent for any key.

functional._comment: The templated element's own functional section, in gabarit form.
functional._key_note: Example only, remove. An empty list or absent value means this key exists on the templated element but its value is unconstrained by this schema.

subjective._comment: The templated element's own subjective section, in gabarit form. Most schemas leave this entirely empty — subjective content is rarely constrained.

_subjective_note: Optional. Free-form space for subjective categorization. Add any key-value pairs meaningful to you or your team — tags, priority, notes, author opinions. The engine ignores this section entirely.
